ev.q: CDC analyzed 2008 data from 121,020 routine pool inspections conducted by a convenience sample of 15 state and local agencies.
Analysis of routine pool inspection data from a convenience sample of 15 jurisdictions with 121,020 inspections
Of 120,975 inspections, 12,917 (10.7%) identified disinfectant level violations.
A total of 13,532 (12.1%) of 111,487 inspections identified serious violations that threatened the public's health
Of 111,487 inspections, 13,532 (12.1%) resulted in immediate closure because of serious violations
Among venues with known pool settings, child-care pool inspections had the highest percentage of immediate closures (17.2%)
Interactive fountain inspections had the highest percentage of immediate closures (17.0%)
Analysis of routine pool inspection data from a convenience sample of 15 jurisdictions with 121,020 inspections
Although these results likely are not representative of all pools in the United States

methods_quotes.q: A violation was defined as an inspection item that did not meet standards set by the jurisdiction's pool code.
CDC developed an algorithm based on facility name to classify pool setting
Because pool codes and, therefore, inspection items, differed across jurisdictions, reported denominators varied.
